post.text:
🚨🇺🇸🇸🇦Jeffrey Epstein placed the sacred Kiswah of the Kaaba on the floor after it was shipped to him directly from Saudi Arabia.

An act many Muslims view as a serious desecration of one of Islam’s holiest symbols. https://t.co/S1AFXiG47H

description.description: A man in a white striped shirt and tan pants is standing next to Jeffrey Epstein in a large room. They are looking down at a large, ornate rug laid out on the floor. In the background, there is a staircase with an iron railing, a red chair, a wooden armchair, and a dark bronze-colored sculpture.

A low-angle shot of the Kaaba in Mecca, showing the black Kiswah silk covering adorned with intricate gold-embroidered Arabic calligraphy. The sun is shining brightly directly above the cube-shaped structure, and a crowd of pilgrims wearing white caps is visible at the bottom of the frame, some reaching out to touch the building.

botInput.comments:
- **Emelia (@wasalive22)**: "Repeating a lie does not turn it into truth. Jeffrey Epstein did not receive the Kaaba’s Kiswah from Saudi Arabia, nor was it shipped to him from there. Official U.S. Department of Justice documents clearly show that the person who handed over the piece was the Emirati shown in the photo, not any Saudi authority. Stop exploiting sacred symbols and distorting facts. Read the documents before spreading falsehoods. Facts silence lies no matter how loud the noise." (Likes: 256)
- **سند (@ii3snd)**: "This claim is misleading and inaccurate. The piece of the Kiswah shown in the photo was not “shipped directly from Saudi Arabia to Jeffrey Epstein” as claimed. It was part of the annual tradition of distributing pieces of the old Kiswah after it is replaced. The specific piece in question was reportedly gifted by an Emirati official, not sent directly by the Saudi government. There is an important difference between an official state shipment and a private gift passed through an intermediary. Accuracy matters." (Likes: 238)
- **د.ابتسام الحربي🇸🇦 (@Dr_Ebtesam_)**: "Why are you lying? What you’re saying contradicts how you present yourself. What are you trying to achieve by lying? That’s wrong. The item was not shipped from Saudi Arabia—the Emirati official standing next to it gave it to him, and it was shipped from the UAE. Saudi government gifts pieces of the old Kiswa to visiting Muslim leaders, and other high-ranking officials in Muslim countries as a token of honor. And it seems that UAE official gave his to EPSTEIN!!" (Likes: 224)
- **نــجــد (@n25d_)**: "The Kaaba’s covering is not only in Saudi Arabia By tradition it is replaced every year, then parts of it are cut and gifted to Islamic countries Whoever neglects or mishandles the gifted portion is the one who bears the responsibility for that action" (Likes: 49)
- **Al-Intellius (@Al_Intellius)**: "They hate Islam. Islam is their biggest enemy. What does that tell you?" (Likes: 49)
- **Eng. Faisal Alotaibi المسافر راح 🇸🇦 (@FaisalAloTaib9)**: "This claim is misleading. It omits well documented context about how the Kiswah of the Kaaba is handled every year. Each year in Mecca the Kiswah is ceremonially replaced as part of an established religious and administrative process overseen by the relevant authorities in Saudi Arabia. When the Kiswah is changed portions of the previous cloth are carefully cut and distributed as official gifts to Muslim countries dignitaries and institutions around the world. This practice has existed for many years and is not unique to any one person or country. The specific piece shown here was not specially shipped from Saudi Arabia to Jeffrey Epstein and it was not an exclusive gesture directed at him. This piece was part of the annual distribution that was officially gifted to the United Arab Emirates as one of many Islamic countries that receive such pieces. The United Arab Emirates later presented this piece to him as a gift. The origin of the gift to him was therefore the UAE not Saudi Arabia. It is incorrect to suggest that Saudi Arabia singled him out or directly honored him with this sacred cloth. Saudi authorities distribute portions of the Kiswah broadly and routinely without distinction among Muslim nations. Many heads of state religious institutions and official buildings around the world display similar pieces in respected settings. The claim that this was a direct shipment from Saudi Arabia to him as a special honor is false. The piece came through the standard annual gifting process to the UAE and was then passed on by Emirati authorities. This clarification helps prevent misrepresentation of a long standing religious tradition." (Likes: 39)
